sections.html:
Newton is a city in Middlesex County, about 8 miles west of downtown Boston. It is made up of thirteen villages rather than one center: Auburndale, Chestnut Hill, Newton Centre, Newton Corner, Newton Highlands, Newton Lower Falls, Newton Upper Falls, Newtonville, Nonantum, Oak Hill, Thompsonville, Waban and West Newton.

Your village shapes your ZIP code, your commute and the kind of house on your street, but it does not change who bills your tax. That is the city's Assessing and Treasury offices. Because streetcar lines, the railroad and later the car brought building in waves, the housing stock is mixed in age, and older houses often come with aging roofs and heating systems that buyers ask about.

Demand stays steady. Colleges, a hospital, the MBTA Green Line, the Worcester commuter rail, the Massachusetts Turnpike and Route 9 all keep buyers interested in Newton houses.

Newton splits the work between two offices. Assessing sets values and handles abatements and exemptions. The Treasury Department bills and collects the real estate tax.

OfficeWhat it handlesHow to reach it
AssessingValues, abatements, exemptions, tax mailing addressCity Hall, Room 111, 1000 Commonwealth Avenue, Newton Centre, MA 02459. 617-796-1160, assessing@newtonma.gov. Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
TreasuryPayments, balances, duplicate bills, refunds, municipal lien certificates, tax title617-796-1330, treasury@newtonma.gov

Pick the right door. If you want to know why your value went up, go to Assessing. If you want to know whether last quarter's payment posted, go to Treasury.

For fiscal year 2026 the certified rates are $9.69 per $1,000 of assessed value for residential property and $18.06 per $1,000 for commercial, industrial and personal property. Your own bill may differ from the plain rate times value because of exemptions or abatements.

  • Rates are set each fiscal year, so next year's bill will use a different number.
  • The rate multiplies your assessed value, which is why an abatement based on value can change what you owe.
  • The city's Assessor's Database and map lets you look up your parcel and see its assessed value.

sections.h2: When is Newton property tax due?
sections.html:
Bills are quarterly, due on the first business day of August, November, February and May.

  • August 1 and November 1: the first two installments of the fiscal year.
  • February 1 and May 1: the final two installments.
  • Motor vehicle excise bills are due within 30 days of issue. Utility bills are issued quarterly and due within 30 days of the bill date.

The first installment date also starts the abatement clock, so it matters beyond paying. An abatement application must be filed with assessors on or before the due date of the first installment of the actual tax bill. In quarterly billing communities that is generally February 1. The face of your tax bill shows the exact dates.

If you think the value on your bill is too high, you apply for an abatement through Newton's Assessing office. Two habits protect your case: file the form before the deadline, and keep paying the installments while you wait. The state's Appellate Tax Board guide treats three things as essential: paying by each due date, filing the abatement form on time, and filing any later appeal with the Board on time.

Once the application is in, assessors have three months to respond. Silence counts as a denial after three calendar months. From the date of their decision, or of that deemed denial, you get another three months to take the matter to the Appellate Tax Board.

Expect to carry the proof. An assessment starts out presumed valid, and it reflects values as of January 1 before the fiscal year, so a fiscal year 2025 bill reflects a January 1, 2024 date. Sales of similar nearby homes are the usual evidence.

  • Pay every installment by its due date, even with an abatement pending.
  • File the form with Assessing before the deadline printed on your bill.
  • Gather photos, your property record card and sales of similar homes.
  • Write down the dates you filed and any reply, so the three-month clock is easy to track.

A few narrow exceptions to the payment rule exist, so read the guide before you decide to skip a payment.

Newton offers exemption, deferral, work-off and assistance programs for eligible taxpayers. Applications for the next fiscal year, FY2027, are available, and exemption applications are due on or before April 1, 2027. After that date, expect the same April 1 cycle each year.

Call Assessing to find out which program fits your age, income or status. If you are selling, ask whether any exemption or deferral on the property changes your closing payoff, and have your closing attorney request the payoff figure.

sections.h2: Before you list or sell as-is
sections.html:
A little preparation with the two city offices saves time once you have a buyer. Here is what to gather.

  • Your latest tax bill, showing the installment dates and any unpaid quarter.
  • Your property record card from the Assessor's Database, so you know how the city describes the house.
  • Any exemption or deferral paperwork, in case it affects what is owed at closing.
  • Notes on any open abatement, including the date you filed.

Timing matters too. Quarterly bills mean a sale in the middle of a fiscal year splits the year between you and the buyer, and the closing attorney sorts that out on the settlement statement. Ask early so the numbers do not surprise you at the table.

A cash sale skips the bank appraisal and the buyer's mortgage approval, which are the steps that most often stall a Newton sale of an older house. The tax work above still applies, but there is less to coordinate.

Treasury is the office to ask about any balance before a sale. It handles municipal lien certificate requests and can explain tax title, redemptions and municipal lien releases.

  1. Ask Treasury what you owe, including any quarter still open.
  2. Request the municipal lien certificate through Treasury so the buyer's side can see the balance.
  3. Ask Assessing for your current assessment and whether an abatement is open.
  4. Tell your closing attorney how you want the balance paid. It is normally settled from the sale proceeds at closing.

If your account is far behind, ask Treasury how tax title and redemption work, and start that conversation early. Waiting only adds to what a buyer's lawyer has to sort out.

Cash Home Buyers buys Newton houses as-is, with no repairs and no listing. If you want an offer on a house with taxes due, reach out. Any tax payoff is handled through closing.

faqs.q: Who sends my Newton property tax bill?
faqs.a: The city's Treasury Department bills and collects the tax, while Assessing sets the value. Treasury can be reached at 617-796-1330.

faqs.q: When are Newton property taxes due?
faqs.a: Quarterly, on the first business day of August, November, February and May.

faqs.q: What is the Newton residential tax rate?
faqs.a: The certified FY2026 rate is $9.69 per $1,000 of assessed value for residential property and $18.06 for commercial, industrial and personal property.

faqs.q: What is the abatement deadline in Newton?
faqs.a: An abatement application is due by the first installment due date on the bill, generally February 1 in quarterly billing communities. Check your bill or call Assessing at 617-796-1160 for the exact date.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Newton house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes, but ask your closing attorney how the balance will be paid. Treasury handles municipal lien certificate requests and can tell you what you owe.
